metadata.review_title: LIKE GOLDILOCKS SAYS -- NOT TOO BIG, NOT TOO SMALL, THEY'RE JUST RIGHT!!!

review_text:
I just got these and I read other reviews before I purchased them and feel there needs to be a more adequate description as to how big these dies are. So here goes.

The base letter with no upper or lower loops is approximately 1/2". Upper extensions such as "l, h, or d" add approximately 1/2". Lower extensions such a "f, p, or g" add approximately 1/2". So . . . in the word "together", where you have both upper and lower extensions added to your base word, it would total 1-1/2". These measurements make it seem like it might be too big for an A2 card. In actuality, they look rather diminutive. Don't let the 1-1/2" measurement deter you from buying this set. It is a very nice collection of words. They are just the right size to get your words noticed without being overbearing in your overall design.

I bought this set solely for the two words "together forever" to use them for wedding cards I'm making. I like this set so much, I plan to purchase the other Tim Holtz word sets (I think there are a total of five more sets to include 1) Christmas words, 2) vacation words, 3) Adventure words, 4) Celebration words and 5) and Daily words with days of the week.). I love the fact that all of the words use the same script so they can be mised and matched with each other.

I hope this additional information helps you to make the decision to buy this set.

metadata.review_title: Goldfaber are Golden! Lovely to Work With.. Hopeful of More Colors to Come!

review_text:
Goldfaber are Golden! Watching tutorials (dangerous warning) I came across one on this great little set of Goldfaber Faber-Castell.. 48 count! I was very impressed! These pencils are simply beautiful as far presentation goes.. they are well made and the thickness is lovely to hold! They came in a nice, easy to open, hinged tin, with the expected plastic trays to hold pencils.. the only difference is the elastic on the sides (pic included) to lift out instead of the finger wedges to lift out.. I LOVED the elastic.. BRAVO Faber-Castell! It's much more stable in keeping pencils in the trays so they don't fall out and easier to lift out.. ESPECIALLY for those with arthritis like me!
In the tutorial (should you be interested in this info) it had stated that as far as Faber-Castell goes.. the red packaging is more for younger school age, the blue for more beginner, older students and the green (polychromos) for the more serious, professional artist.. which I'm not.. I'm a hobbyist & I LOVE to color.. so I couldn't wait to try these out.. next on my list is the Polychromos.. I've tried one just they cost a pretty penny!
I wasn't so keen on the red packaged Faber-Castell Pencils.. they were just ok but couldn't even compete with these Goldfabers! They worked beautifully with other pencils, blenders & mineral spirits. Little dust, very little if any wax bloom (I personally didn't get any but others have said they had), layered wonderfully.. GREAT value for your money.. my only con this far is the biggest set you can get is 48.. I do hope they add more to the Goldfaber Collection.. but to leave on a positive note, although the pencils don't have names, they do have numbers and can be replaced as needed with open stock availability.. YAY.. which isn't the case with most pencils!
UPDATE: I'm not going to take away stars since it could just be a defective tin.. and these pencils are lovely (I wish there was a larger set).. as I've been using my pencils and waiting for my pencil case to arrive I've noticed my tin doesn't stay shut very well.. no harm to my pencils but maybe don't depend on the tin so much. 😉

metadata.review_title: Works okay for displaying items, but definitely not as an easle for lightweight artwork in process

review_text: These were just okay.  They'd probably work well displaying really small, lightweight items, but nothing much larger than a 4x6/ 5x7.  I purchased them for my daughter's art party and was hoping it would have worked with our super lightweight, wood-free 8x10 canvases, but it didn't.  We tried it with some 5x7 lightweight canvases as well, which it held, but even the lightest pressure from a paintbrush causes it to topple over.  If you're just looking to display some lightweight items, it should work well for you.  If you're displaying lightweight items that will be touched here and there and/or have any pressure whatsoever applied including from a breeze, opt for something larger and more sturdy.

The colors are not listed on the stick so if you run out and want more it’s hard. And once the film dries on them it’s hard to tell what color is what.  My set was not complete as I had two blues and no black.  Disappointing. I like the product but they need to work on it.

On the surface these corners are lovely. They have an antique stamped finish that provides an attractive corner.

These are glued on, not nailed-- which is great if you like working with epoxy, not so great if you prefer an authentic hammered-nail appearance (individual preference). There are no nail holes, nor nails included.

However there are several disadvantages to this product:

* It's not a true "corner" that covers the entire corner of the box. It is a stamp-cut and bent piece of sheet metal, leaving a v-grove in the corner and the corner side exposed.
* The corner is quite pointed and sharp-- so much so that it is not something I would choose to use again.
* This isn't one color, but is rather three slightly-different colors, approximating antique dull silver, gold and brass. That means if one wishes to do all 8 corners of a box the same color, you will need two sets of these corners. While it does say this in the *secondary* description, that information is not included in the main description. The color differences are very subtle (you can see it in the package photo if you look closely).
* The price on this item increased some 40% within one week.

Since boxes have 8 corners, it makes me wonder why they don't package these 8 or 16 in a pack and sell them in single colors. It seems this 12-corner 3-color set is designed either for projects that only use 4 corners, or to sell 2 packages at a time. I purchased 2 packages of these and was glad I did. Had I not I wouldn't have appreciated that vital information lacking in the main description and having to order a second package to complete my project.

General overall opinion: attractive but low-quality and SHARP (as in ouch) corners that require buying 2 sets to corner one box. As stamped and bent sheet metal I consider this over-priced. I will be opting for a little better-quality item next order. These are beautiful, but for a good box with "safe" corners, imo not the best option.

metadata.review_title: Works great, but does NOT do 72 projects

review_text: This block party kit does not do anywhere near 72 projects (unless you're doing something much smaller than shirts, maybe?). We had to run to craft stores to round up more dye mid-project when we realized we were going to come up really short. But, other than that, it's great! Super easy to use and lots of fun! It has clear instructions for the process, plus directions to make different patterns. We let the dyed shirts sit overnight before we rinsed them, and I was surprised by how well they held their color! We used some smaller bottles to mix additional colors, too.
